_note: Draft EDOP signature schema — April 2026. Dummy instance for Ur (30.9626N, 46.1033E). Values are illustrative; some approximate from prior analysis. Fields marked [*] not yet implemented.

period._note: D band suppressed for pre-industrial period. Temporal datasets queried where available.

A_physiographic._note: Bedrock physical character; stable over geological timescales

B_hydroclimatic._note: s = local sub-basin; near_u = decay-weighted near-upstream aggregate [*]; u = full upstream catchment

C_bioclimatic._note: Proxies for ecological and land-surface conditions

D_anthropocene._note: Modern-era markers; suppress or qualify for pre-industrial analysis

divergence._note: s/u ratio per variable; values > 1 indicate drier/warmer/etc. locally than upstream

scale_sensitivity._note: How much the local (s) signature changes between basin levels [*]

temporal._note: [*] Period-specific climate context from LMR v2.1 (Tardif et al. 2019). Gridded reanalysis, 2°×2°, 20-member MC ensemble. Values are actual extractions for Ur (30.0N, 46.0E), 900–1000 CE.

pdsi._note: Palmer Drought Severity Index; 0 = climatological mean, negative = drier, positive = wetter
pdsi._decadal_note: 900s and 910s from confirmed extraction; remaining decades [*] pending full run

air_temperature._note: [*] Surface air temperature anomaly relative to 1961–1990 baseline; °C

sst._note: Sea surface temperature — not applicable for inland location

coverage._note: Documents data sources and temporal basis for each signature component. Never omitted; fields are null when not yet implemented.

dendrochronology.source: PAGES 2k v2.0.0 — point records only, not yet integrated

narrative: [*] Ur occupies a hyper-arid local environment (aridity index 5, 94mm/yr precipitation) fed by an upstream catchment receiving over four times the local rainfall — a sharp local/upstream divergence characteristic of alluvial civilizations dependent on distant water sources. The site lies approximately 890km upstream from the Persian Gulf, close enough for maritime access while insulated from direct tidal influence. Terrestrial conditions alone would predict marginal viability; the combination of upstream water delivery and downstream sea access explains the site's historical centrality.
